title: Two Sum II — Sorted Input
description: Find two numbers in a sorted array that sum to a target using converging pointers and O(1) space.

data.text: Given a **1-indexed, sorted** array `numbers`, find two values that add up to `target` and return their 1-based indices. Exactly one solution exists, and you may not use the same element twice.

**Input:** `numbers = [2, 7, 11, 15]`, `target = 9`

**Output:** `[1, 2]`

**Explanation:** `2 + 7 = 9`, so the answer uses the first and second elements.
The unsorted Two Sum solution uses a dictionary of seen values. It works here too, but it ignores the fact that the input is sorted and costs O(n) extra memory for no benefit.

data.title: Hash Map O(n) time, O(n) space
data.content: Works but wastes the sorted property.

data.text: Because the array is sorted, put `left` at the start and `right` at the end. Compute the sum. If it is too small, the only way to increase it is to move `left` right. If it is too large, the only way to decrease it is to move `right` left. Each pointer moves at most n times, so the loop is O(n) with O(1) space.

data.title: Two Pointers O(n) time, O(1) space
data.content: Converge from both ends using the sorted order.

data.title: The monotonic argument
data.text: Sorted order gives you a guarantee: if `numbers[left] + numbers[right]` is too small, then pairing `numbers[left]` with any element at or before `right` is also too small. That is why it is always safe to move `left` — you never skip over a valid answer.

data.title: Return 1-based indices
data.text: The problem statement is explicit that indices are 1-based. Off-by-one errors here are the single most common wrong answer on this problem in interviews.

data.caption: Pointers converge: too small moves left forward, too large moves right backward, until the sum matches.
data.definition:
graph LR
    A["[2,7,11,15] target=9"] --> B["left=0 right=3 sum=17 > 9"]
    B --> C["right-- : left=0 right=2 sum=13 > 9"]
    C --> D["right-- : left=0 right=1 sum=9 == target"]
    D --> E["return [1,2]"]
    style E fill:#e8f5e9,stroke:#2e7d32

data.title: Complete solution
data.content: This converging-pointer template is reused for '3Sum', 'container with most water', and 'valid palindrome'. Whenever input is sorted and you are looking for a pair with a property, converging pointers should be your first instinct.
